intended_object: A fixed list of ten lattice points (the centre and some boundary vertices of a target region). The proof of the Conway–Soifer covering result uses it to give each covering triangle a distinct "owner" point. This comes from the docstring and from how the library uses it (`anchored`, `anchors_separated`).
explanation: The definition is a hard-coded table of ten points in ℤ²-coordinates. It is only an auxiliary device inside the formalized proof of the Conway–Soifer problem. Its role is to fix, for each of the ten covering triangles, a point that the triangle must contain. The library checks that these points lie in the target region (`anchor_mem_target`) and that any two of them are at squared distance at least 1 (`anchors_separated`). Neither the literature nor Mathlib has a standard mathematical object of which this would be a formalization. It is internal proof data.
